newsitem.title: FRANCE: Franco-Italian summit set for October 3-4.
newsitem.headline: Franco-Italian summit set for October 3-4.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will meet on October 3-4 in a summit likely to focus on European Union institutional reform and Rome's bid to qualify for a single currency, officials said.

EU reform will be high on the agenda as the meeting will start just days before a special EU summit, set for Dublin on October 5, on the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC), which many in the 15-member bloc believe has bogged down.

An Italian diplomat said Rome's efforts not to miss out on the European single currency and to stick as close as possible to the 1992 Maastricht criteria for monetary union would also be part of the talks.
The French Foreign Ministry, which announced the dates, did not say where the Franco-Italian summit would take place.
But French officials said in June that Chirac and Prodi had agreed to hold a bilateral summit soon in an Italian city.
The officials said at the time that the summit would tackle defence and security policy, immigration and cultural issues.

Chirac and Prodi last met in Paris on June 10. After a luncheon, the two leaders said they had agreed to a new era of warm Franco-Italian friendship, ending a period of troubled ties due to French nuclear tests.

After Italy and several other EU partners backed a United Nations resolution condemning the South Pacific tests, France -- in a fit of pique -- had retaliated by cancelling a previous summit planned for Sicily last November.
France ended the series of nuclear tests in January.
Chirac had also clashed repeatedly with Prodi's predecessor Lamberto Dini, accusing him of engineering a competitive devaluation of the lira which hurt French exports.
